spec: CONTROL.md §6, A session is the one its harness filed under that id
note: Which Claude Code session a ref names, from the transcripts on disk: `filed` are the names of the files in one project folder, `asked` is the id a command names. `found` is the file that is that session's transcript, or null: no session of this machine's, acked `refused` with `no_session`. It is the file of exactly that name, whatever a file system that ignores case would open for another spelling: the session's registry row and its hooks are kept under the id as its harness wrote it, so a session reached by another spelling has a transcript and nothing that says it is held. `taken` is the other question, asked for a `start`: whether a new session of that id would collide with one that exists, which it does in any spelling (`bad_session`).

cases.name: in upper case: found by no machine, and not free for a new session
a session its harness filed in upper case is found as that, and not as lower case
the same asked for in lower case
the id with another ending is not the transcript
